findings.issue_text: app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:141–143 compares hosts after dropping their first label, incorrectly treating unrelated domains such as example.co.uk and other.co.uk as the same domain and displaying the full path. Compare registrable domains using public-suffix rules.

app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:138 compares hostnames case-sensitively despite DNS hostnames being case-insensitive, causing https://EXAMPLE.com/user to display only EXAMPLE.com for instance example.com. Normalize hostname case before comparison.

goldens.comment: The include_website_name method is missing the required ? suffix. Rails serializers expect include_ methods to end with ? for conditional attribute inclusion, a convention followed by other methods in this serializer. Without it, the website_name attribute may not be conditionally included as intended. Additionally, the '.' << website_host string concatenation should be replaced with '.' + website_host or '.#{website_host}' to avoid mutating string literals, which can lead to issues.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:141–143 compares hosts after dropping their first label, incorrectly treating unrelated domains such as example.co.uk and other.co.uk as the same domain and displaying the full path. Compare registrable domains using public-suffix rules.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies a real bug in the domain comparison logic at lines 141-143. The code compares domains by dropping the first label (e.g., 'www' or 'forum') and comparing the rest. This means 'example.co.uk' and 'other.co.uk' would both become 'co.uk' after dropping the first label, causing them to be incorrectly treated as the same domain. The condition `website_host.split('.')[1..-1].join('.') == discourse_host.split('.')[1..-1].join('.')` is flawed because it doesn't account for public suffix rules (like .co.uk being a single suffix). This would cause the full path to be displayed for unrelated domains that happen to share a common suffix.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:138 compares hostnames case-sensitively despite DNS hostnames being case-insensitive, causing https://EXAMPLE.com/user to display only EXAMPLE.com for instance example.com. Normalize hostname case before comparison.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows hostname comparisons at lines 140-148 using direct string equality (==) and ends_with? without any case normalization. DNS hostnames are case-insensitive per RFC, so 'EXAMPLE.com' should match 'example.com'. The code compares website_host == discourse_host directly, which would fail for mixed-case URLs. This is a real correctness bug in the new website_name method.
